evidence.statement: Frozen cluster COL-0001 contains a three-token same-diagonal architecture shared by E. coli and yeast mitochondrial DNA: LC-PRIM-0007, then LC-PRIM-0003 exactly 1,370 bp later, then LC-PRIM-0006 exactly 119 bp later.
All three yeast token starts fall inside the recorded mitochondrial 21S_RRNA/Q0158 locus.

COL-0001 is therefore a literal three-symbol bacterial↔mitochondrial grammar candidate with one side semantically localized to mitochondrial large-subunit rRNA; the E. coli side is intentionally not promoted until assembly-matched annotation is checked.
Post-freeze validation confirms the E. coli three-token COL-0001 coordinates all lie within rrlA 23S rRNA; the corresponding yeast coordinates all lie within mitochondrial 21S rRNA.
LC-GRAM-0004 is therefore a validated three-token colinear large-subunit-rRNA architecture shared between bacterial 23S rRNA and mitochondrial 21S rRNA.

Functional mapping shows the three-token grammar traverses a central-core boundary token (LC-PRIM-0007), an intersubunit-interface token (LC-PRIM-0003), and a PTC-neighborhood token (LC-PRIM-0006). This is a systems-level structural mapping; it does not prove the three tokens are one biochemical instruction.
